description: Comparing DNA and protein sequences computationally: sequence formats and databases, pairwise alignment by dynamic programming, substitution matrices and gap penalties, BLAST database search and its statistics, multiple sequence alignment, motifs and profiles, and hidden Markov models for sequence families. Practised by implementing the core algorithms in the browser and applying them to public data such as the haemoglobin beta gene behind sickle cell disease and Plasmodium falciparum drug-resistance genes.
modelledOn: Durbin, Eddy, Krogh and Mitchison, Biological Sequence Analysis: Probabilistic Models of Proteins and Nucleic Acids
Mount, Bioinformatics: Sequence and Genome Analysis
Jones and Pevzner, An Introduction to Bioinformatics Algorithms
outcomes: Retrieve, parse and convert nucleotide and protein sequences in FASTA, GenBank and FASTQ formats and navigate the major public sequence databases.
Derive and implement global, local and semi-global alignment by dynamic programming, including affine gap penalties and traceback.
Explain how PAM and BLOSUM substitution matrices are built from log-odds scores and choose matrices and gap penalties suited to a comparison.
Search sequence databases with BLAST and interpret bit scores, E-values and alignment coverage when judging homology.
Construct and assess multiple sequence alignments and summarise conserved regions as consensus sequences, position weight matrices and sequence logos.
Build and apply hidden Markov models with the Viterbi, forward and Baum-Welch algorithms to gene finding and protein family classification.

units.title: Biological sequences, formats and databases
topics: From the central dogma to data: DNA, RNA and protein alphabets; codons, reading frames and translation
Sequence file formats: FASTA, GenBank flat files, FASTQ with Phred quality scores; parsing them in code
Primary and curated databases: GenBank, ENA, RefSeq, UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot, Ensembl; accession numbers and versions
Basic sequence operations: reverse complement, GC content, k-mer counting, open reading frame finding
Retrieving the human HBB gene with the sickle cell mutation (Glu6Val) and Plasmodium falciparum genes from public databases

units.title: Dot plots and the alignment problem
topics: Why align: homology, similarity and identity distinguished; orthologues and paralogues
Dot plots with windows and stringency; spotting repeats, inversions and domain duplications
Edit distance and the alignment as a path through a grid; how many possible alignments there are
Recursion with memoisation versus tabulation; why brute force fails

units.title: Pairwise alignment with dynamic programming
topics: Needleman-Wunsch global alignment: recurrence, initialisation, filling the matrix, traceback
Smith-Waterman local alignment and semi-global (overlap) alignment; when each is appropriate
Affine gap penalties with Gotoh's three-matrix algorithm; gap opening versus extension
Time and space complexity; linear-space alignment with Hirschberg's divide and conquer
Banded alignment for long similar sequences; implementing and visualising each algorithm step by step

units.title: Scoring matrices and gap penalties
topics: Scoring as log-odds: target frequencies, background frequencies and the meaning of a score
PAM matrices from closely related sequences and extrapolation by matrix powers; Dayhoff's evolutionary model
BLOSUM matrices from conserved blocks; how clustering thresholds define BLOSUM62 and its relatives
Nucleotide scoring schemes, transition and transversion weighting; choosing a matrix for the divergence at hand
Statistical significance of alignment scores: extreme value distribution, Karlin-Altschul statistics, permutation tests

units.title: Database search with BLAST
topics: Heuristic search: word seeding, neighbourhood words, two-hit extension and gapped extension in BLAST; FASTA in brief
BLAST programs: blastn, blastp, blastx, tblastn, tblastx and megablast; choosing the right one
Interpreting results: raw and bit scores, E-values, percentage identity, query coverage; the effect of database size
Low-complexity filtering, repeat masking and avoiding false positives
Iterative profile search with PSI-BLAST; the risk of profile drift
Identifying an unknown pathogen sequence or a resistance gene such as pfcrt or pfkelch13 by BLAST

units.title: Multiple sequence alignment
topics: Why multiple alignment is hard: the sum-of-pairs objective and NP-hardness
Progressive alignment: guide trees, profile-profile alignment and why early gaps are frozen (Clustal)
Iterative refinement and consistency-based methods: MUSCLE, MAFFT, T-Coffee
Evaluating alignments against benchmarks; trimming unreliable columns
Visualising and editing alignments; conservation scores across malaria antigen variants

units.title: Motifs and profiles
topics: Consensus sequences, regular-expression patterns and PROSITE
Position frequency and position weight matrices; pseudocounts; information content and sequence logos
Scanning sequences with a weight matrix for transcription factor binding sites
Motif discovery by expectation maximisation (MEME) and Gibbs sampling
Protein domains and family databases: Pfam and InterPro

units.title: Hidden Markov models for sequences
topics: Markov chains for sequences: CpG islands and log-likelihood ratio scoring
Hidden Markov models: states, transitions, emissions; the occasionally dishonest casino
Viterbi decoding, the forward and backward algorithms, posterior decoding; working in log space
Parameter estimation by counting and by Baum-Welch expectation maximisation
Profile HMMs with match, insert and delete states; HMMER searches against Pfam
Gene finding with HMMs: exons, introns and splice signals

units.title: Applications and project
topics: Reproducible sequence analysis with Biopython and notebooks; recording tool versions and parameters
Comparing HBB variants across populations and relating sequence change to protein change
Annotating a newly sequenced gene: search, align, identify domains, predict function
Project: an alignment and annotation report on a gene of public health importance in Africa

schedule.title: Sequences as data
schedule.exercise: Translate a short DNA sequence in all six frames by hand and explain how the HBB sickle cell mutation changes codon 6.

tasks.title: Compute reverse complement, GC content and 3-mer counts for a 60-base sequence and check each against hand counts
Parse a FASTQ file of 20 reads, convert Phred scores to error probabilities and drop reads with mean quality below 20
Find all open reading frames of at least 100 codons in a 3000-base sequence on both strands and report their coordinates and protein lengths

schedule.title: Why and how to compare sequences
schedule.exercise: Count by hand how many ways two 4-letter sequences can be aligned and explain why the number explodes.

tasks.title: Draw a dot plot of two 40-base sequences with a repeat, and mark the diagonal that shows the repeat and the one that shows an inversion
Fill an edit distance table for two 6-letter words step by step and trace one optimal path back through the grid
Implement edit distance by plain recursion, by memoisation and by tabulation and compare call counts and runtime for lengths up to 20

schedule.title: Dynamic programming alignment
schedule.exercise: Align two short protein fragments by hand with Needleman-Wunsch and then with Smith-Waterman, and say which answer suits a domain search.

tasks.title: Fill the Needleman-Wunsch matrix for two 6-base sequences with given scores and trace back the optimal global alignment
Align a short motif inside a longer sequence with Smith-Waterman and semi-global modes, and compare the alignments each reports
Implement Gotoh's affine-gap alignment with three matrices, test it on 8 pairs and show how raising the gap open penalty changes results

schedule.title: Efficient alignment algorithms
schedule.exercise: Compare time and memory of full and linear-space alignment for sequences of 1000 and 100000 bases, in a short table.

tasks.title: Plot the cells filled and memory used for sequence lengths 100 to 5000 with quadratic and linear-space alignment, and read off where memory fails
Run banded alignment on two 20-base sequences with a band of 3 and compare the score against the full matrix
Implement Hirschberg's divide and conquer alignment, verify it returns the same score as the full matrix on 10 pairs and measure memory saved

schedule.title: Scoring matrices and significance
schedule.exercise: Derive a log-odds score for one amino acid pair from target and background frequencies and say what a positive score means.

tasks.title: Compute log-odds scores for five amino acid pairs from given frequencies and compare them with the matching BLOSUM62 entries
Raise a PAM1 matrix to the powers 30 and 250 and observe how identity probabilities fall and the substitution pattern flattens
Shuffle one sequence 1000 times, align each against a fixed query, fit an extreme value distribution and report a p-value for the true score

schedule.title: Database search with BLAST
schedule.exercise: Pick the right BLAST program for four queries, such as a new cDNA, a protein and a genome contig, and explain each choice.

tasks.title: Choose between blastn, blastp, blastx and tblastn for six query-database pairs and justify each against the program's translation rules
Step through BLAST seeding on a query with word size 3, list neighbourhood words, find two-hit seeds and extend one to a high-scoring pair
Read a hit table of 10 results, convert raw to bit scores, compute E-values for two database sizes and explain how the ranking changes

schedule.title: Filtering, profiles and identification
schedule.exercise: Explain how low-complexity regions can produce high scores with no homology and how profile drift can contaminate PSI-BLAST.

tasks.title: Mask low-complexity stretches in a protein sequence by entropy in a sliding window and count how many false hits the masking removes
Build a position-specific scoring matrix from 10 aligned homologues and use it to score 5 candidate sequences, ranking them
Identify an unknown pathogen sequence and a resistance gene variant by searching a reference set, and report the best hit with evidence

schedule.title: Multiple sequence alignment
schedule.exercise: Score a 4-sequence alignment with the sum-of-pairs objective by hand and explain why exact optimisation is infeasible for 30 sequences.

tasks.title: Compute the sum-of-pairs score of a 4-sequence alignment for each column and the total using a given scoring matrix
Build a guide tree from pairwise distances of 5 sequences and align them progressively, showing the profile merges in order
Refine a progressive alignment by iterative repartitioning and realignment, and report how the sum-of-pairs score improves each round

schedule.title: Evaluating and using alignments
schedule.exercise: Judge a 12-sequence alignment of a malaria antigen by eye, mark unreliable columns and propose what to trim.

tasks.title: Compute a per-column conservation score for an alignment of 10 antigen variants and list the five most conserved positions
Compare a test alignment with a benchmark reference using sum-of-pairs and column scores, then trim columns with over 50 percent gaps
Plot conservation along a malaria antigen and mark variable regions, then explain which regions suit a vaccine target and why

schedule.title: Motifs and domains
schedule.exercise: Build a position weight matrix from eight binding sites by hand and compute the information content of each column.

tasks.title: Build a frequency matrix with pseudocounts from 10 aligned sites, convert to log-odds and compute the score of one candidate site
Scan a 500-base promoter with a weight matrix, report windows above a threshold and compare hits with the known planted site
Implement Gibbs sampling to find a 6-base motif hidden in 10 random 50-base sequences, and report the motif and its recovery rate

schedule.title: Hidden Markov models
schedule.exercise: Run Viterbi by hand on a 5-roll sequence in the dishonest casino model and compare it with posterior decoding.

tasks.title: Build a two-state Markov model of CpG island and background DNA and compute the log-odds score of three given sequences
Run the Viterbi algorithm step by step on a 10-roll sequence from the dishonest casino and read off the most likely state path
Implement forward, backward and posterior decoding in log space for a 3-state HMM and verify the probabilities sum to one at each position

schedule.title: Training HMMs and profile models
schedule.exercise: Sketch a profile HMM for a 5-column alignment with match, insert and delete states and explain what a delete state means biologically.

tasks.title: Estimate HMM transition and emission probabilities by counting from a labelled training sequence and compare them with the true values
Score three sequences against a small profile HMM with match, insert and delete states, showing the best path for each
Train a simple gene-finding HMM with exon, intron and intergenic states using Baum-Welch and report its accuracy on 5 held-out sequences

schedule.title: Reproducible analysis and project
schedule.exercise: Write the methods section of your project report so another student could rerun it, listing tools, versions and parameters.

tasks.title: Write a notebook that loads a FASTA file, aligns two sequences, prints the identity and records parameters and versions in the output
Align HBB variants from 6 populations, locate each substitution and report which change the protein sequence and which are silent
Annotate an unknown gene by searching, aligning with homologues, scanning for domains and proposing a function with supporting evidence
